# OpenPhonex Gateway

> OpenPhonex Gateway — the self-hostable LiveKit media plane behind OpenPhonex: livekit-server + livekit-sip + the production media-plane agent + a session reconciler + redis. Call audio (SIP/RTP) stays on the operator's servers; the OpenPhonex control plane (Cloud or self-hosted) resolves per-call config, authorizes tools, and settles billing over a thin HTTPS bearer-token link. Numbers, KYB/compliance, billing, and abuse policy stay in the control plane.

## Repository map

- [Self-host install runbook](INSTALL.md): the linear, step-by-step self-host guide (prerequisites -> configure -> up -> provision -> smoke test -> test call); every env var documented with what/where-to-get-it/example. START HERE to install.
- [Agent operating instructions](AGENTS.md): how an AI agent should execute the install and work in this repo.
- [Self-host smoke test](packages/openphonex-gateway/deploy/selfhost-smoketest.sh): PASS/FAIL verification of the running stack (services, agent registration, both control-plane tokens); exit 0 proves the safe prerequisites, while the first real call confirms the DID route.
- [LiveKit production agent](livekit_agent/): the production media-plane agent (runtime modules byte-identical to what OpenPhonex production runs; minimal pinned Dockerfile); per-call config resolves from the control plane.
- [Self-host quickstart + deploy files](packages/openphonex-gateway/deploy/SELFHOST.md): runbook, [docker-compose.livekit.yml](packages/openphonex-gateway/deploy/docker-compose.livekit.yml), config templates.
- [openphonex-gateway package](packages/openphonex-gateway/): shared realtime pipeline / provider library (streaming STT-LLM-TTS primitives, semantic audio policy, call evidence) exercised by the exported tests.
- [openphonex-common package](packages/openphonex-common/): control-plane-free shared config + runtime helpers.
- [Gateway↔Cloud contract](contracts/gateway-v1.yaml): OpenAPI v1.0.0, stable.
- [JSON Schemas](contracts/schemas/): request/response bodies for the stable surface.
- [README](README.md): overview and quickstart pointers.

## The LiveKit media plane (matches production)

The self-host stack tracks OpenPhonex production closely but is not identical to it: livekit-server v1.13.5 + livekit-sip v1.7.0 match the production voice box tag-and-digest as of 2026-08-11, while redis 8.8.0 does not (production is on 7.4.5-alpine); all three are digest-pinned + the `agents` container running [livekit_agent/agent/production_agent.py](livekit_agent/agent/production_agent.py) (LiveKit Agents 1.6.6) + a session `reconciler`. The agent joins each inbound room unsubscribed and admits NO caller audio until the control plane authorizes the call: `POST /v1/calls/inbound/route` (the deployment-bound `tgw_` gateway token) resolves the DID to the authoritative agent, then `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}/realtime-config` (the same token) returns the validated semantic config (system prompt, first message, language, Deepgram nova-3 STT, Gemini LLM, ElevenLabs TTS + voice, tool allowlist). Tool schemas come from MCP `tools/list` on `POST /mcp`, are exposed to the model ONLY if allowlisted, and every invocation re-crosses the call-bound `POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/agent-tool-calls` endpoint with an audit trail. Lifecycle events post to `POST /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/call-lifecycle-events` and produce the authoritative billing verdict; artifacts upload to `POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/artifacts`. The reconciler closes sessions whose agent died so dangling billed minutes are impossible.

## The contract (gateway ↔ Cloud)

The exact surface is [contracts/gateway-v1.yaml](contracts/gateway-v1.yaml) (v1.0.0 stable) plus [contracts/schemas/](contracts/schemas/). Endpoints the stack uses:

- `POST /v1/calls/inbound/route` — resolve an inbound DID to the authoritative agent (gateway token).
- `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}/realtime-config` — the validated per-call semantic config (gateway token).
- `POST /mcp` — MCP `tools/list` schema discovery (gateway token; `tools/list` is the only method it may call).
- `POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/agent-tool-calls` — allowlisted model-tool execution bound to that call.
- `POST /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/call-lifecycle-events` — lifecycle + authoritative billing verdict (gateway token).
- `POST /v1/calls/{id}/artifacts` — upload call artifacts with duration provenance (gateway token).
- `POST /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/tokens` / `.../tokens/rotate` — mint / rotate the per-gateway `tgw_` token (shown once).
- `GET /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/number-rules` — routing read (also the smoke test's gateway-token probe).
- `POST /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/outbound-calls` — admit an outbound call THIS deployment will dial (gateway token, `local` mode only). Returns the admitted call plus a single-use `tca_` bound to that call; nothing is enqueued.
- `GET /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}` — read `outbound_execution_mode`: this is how an agent tells which originate path it is on.

## Placing an outbound call (which path am I on?)

A deployment is in one of two outbound modes, readable at
`GET /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}` as `outbound_execution_mode`:

- `local` — this box dials its own calls. Ask it to dial:
  `docker compose -f packages/openphonex-gateway/deploy/docker-compose.livekit.yml run --rm outbound-worker python /app/outbound_worker.py originate --to +<E164> --purpose <purpose> --reason "<why>"`.
  The control plane runs the full policy + wallet admission and mints the
  call-bound token; no organization-scoped key exists on this box, and a remote
  `POST /v1/calls` for this workspace's numbers is refused with a message that
  names this command.
- `queue` (the default, and every deployment created before local origination)
  — outbound calls are requested from the control plane with an
  organization-scoped API key (`POST /v1/calls`) and this box's
  `--profile outbound` worker claims and dials them.

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer` from `OPENPHONEX_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN` (`tgw_...`, narrowly scoped to its registered gateway) — the only runtime credential this stack needs, inbound AND outbound, once the deployment is in `local` outbound mode. Its organization is derived server-side from the token row, never from the request body, and `tools/list` is the only MCP method it may call. `OPENPHONEX_WORKER_API_TOKEN` (`tai_...`, organization-scoped) is needed ONLY by the legacy `queue` outbound mode, where claiming other requesters' call jobs is organization-wide worker-job authority a gateway token deliberately excludes; leave it unset on a `local`-mode box. The transport layer requires https (or verified loopback http) and refuses cross-origin redirects.

## Audio contract

`pcm_s16le_8000_mono` — 16-bit little-endian PCM, 8 kHz, mono. No negotiation.

## Safety boundaries

- The agent admits no caller audio before the control plane authorizes the call and its config validates.
- Tools are model-visible ONLY if allowlisted in realtime-config; every call is auditable at the control plane.
- Bearer tokens never travel plaintext to non-loopback hosts; cross-origin redirects are refused.
- The gateway token is deployment-scoped, so a compromise stops at this deployment's workspace. In `local` outbound mode that is the ONLY credential on the box; the legacy `queue` mode's `tai_` key is organization-scoped and widens that blast radius knowingly. Protect the host, rotate on suspicion ([SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)).
- Outbound origination never bypasses the control plane: this box cannot reach media without a single-use `tca_` the control plane mints only after its own policy decision, caps, kill switches and wallet reserve have passed.
